notes: List used: 2026 Builder 100 (Builder magazine / Zonda), ranked by 2025 closings; all 100 rows captured. builderonline.com returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare bot check) to automated fetches, so the rows were read from the Internet Archive capture of the publisher's own list page dated 2026-11-07 (source_url on each row); confidence is therefore "Reported" for every row even though the capture is a verbatim copy of the publisher table (rank, name, closings, gross revenue in $M, prior-year rank, public/private flag). revenue_usd_m is Builder's "2025 Gross Revenues" (home building revenue, $M); null where Builder shows $0 (builder declined to share). rank_prev null = "N/A" on Builder's table. ownership is Builder's own Public/Private flag unless an enrichment source is listed on the row; Builder flags Sekisui House U.S. as public (parent is listed in Japan). ticker/parent/hq are null unless sourced (see enrichment_source_urls on the row). Cross-check: Pro Builder renamed Housing Giants to the "Top 200"; housing_giants_* fields come from the 2026 Top 200 (published 2026-06-11, ranked by 2025 home building revenue, https://www.probuilder.com/top-200/article/55377310/the-2026-top-200-rankings). Pro Builder ranks by revenue and Builder by closings, so ranks differ by design. Builder 100 companies NOT on Pro Builder 2026 Top 200 (16): Middleburg Communities (#23); AMH (#35); Empire Homes (#61); Holiday Builders (#62); NeighborWorks America (#72); View Homes (#73); Long Lake Ltd. POST-LIST M&A (important): several ranked builders have changed hands since publication - Taylor Morrison (#6) acquired by Berkshire Hathaway (July 2026); Tri Pointe Homes (#19) by Sumitomo Forestry (May 2026); Beazer Homes (#21) by Dream Finders Homes (#14) (closed 2026-10-20); United Homes Group (#56) by Stanley Martin Homes (#18) (May 2026); HistoryMaker Homes (#77) by Century Communities (#10) (October 2026). ownership/ticker/parent on those rows reflect status as of 2026-11-19, not as of publication. Unverified lead (headline seen in search results only, page not opened): Stanley Martin Homes acquired Florida-based Holiday Builders (#62). Thin fields: hq comes from Builder's firm profile pages (Internet Archive captures) where retrievable; ticker/parent only where a page was opened to confirm; many private builders have parent=null meaning "not researched", not "confirmed independent". Web-search budget for this run was exhausted before every ownership question could be checked.
